## Barrier Point Definition

The term "barrier point" means that you first must address this ADKAR element before moving forward in the model. More specifically, the Barrier Point is the first ADKAR element where a person or group scores below 3 (on a 1-5 scale).

## Resistance and Diagnosis

Research participants consistently identify lack of Awareness as the primary reason why employees and managers resist a change. The model uses "Why is this change happening?" as the diagnostic question for identifying an Awareness barrier. Awareness: "Why are we doing this?" needs clearer messaging about the reasons for change

## Sequential Importance

The relationships between ADKAR elements are important because the five building blocks are sequential. A barrier point at Awareness can affect Desire, and a sagging or low level of any one element can pull down other elements.

The search results confirm that Prosci's ADKAR model uses barrier point identification as a diagnostic approach to understanding resistance to change, with a focus on determining where in the five-element sequence (Awareness, Desire, Knowledge, Ability, Reinforcement) an individual or group becomes blocked.

# Prosci / ADKAR — Change Adoption Narrative & Verbatim Copy

## 1. Name & What It Is
**Prosci** is a change-management research and advisory firm; page title: *"Prosci | The Global Leader in Change Management Solutions"*. Its flagship model is the **Prosci ADKAR® Model** — **A**wareness, **D**esire, **K**nowledge, **A**bility, **R**einforcement. Developed by Prosci founder Jeff Hiatt after studying "more than 700 organizations." ADKAR is the individual-change component nested inside the broader **Prosci Methodology** (which also contains the **PCT Model** — Prosci Change Triangle — and the **3-Phase Process**: Prepare Approach → Manage Change → Sustain Outcomes). Brand refresh publicly launched April 2026 ("30 years of leadership").

## 2. Primary URLs
- Homepage: https://www.prosci.com/
- ADKAR: https://www.prosci.com/methodology/adkar
- Methodology overview: https://www.prosci.com/methodology-overview
- ADKAR blog / "people side": https://www.prosci.com/blog/adkar-core-to-the-people-side-of-change , https://www.prosci.com/blog/adkar-model
- PCT Model: https://www.prosci.com/methodology/pct-model
- 2026 strategy: https://www.prosci.com/blog/5-strategic-decisions-for-building-organizational-change-capability
- Brand relaunch: https://www.prosci.com/blog/prosci-evolved-brand

## 3. Narrative / Story Frame
The core story: **technology change fails not for technical reasons but human ones** — so the differentiator is "the people side of change." Change is framed as something that only succeeds when *individuals* transition, one by one, through ADKAR. Resistance is not villainized but **diagnosed** — located at a "barrier point" (the first ADKAR element scoring below 3 on a 1–5 scale), most often **Awareness** ("Why is this change happening?"). Adoption is the payoff word; ROI is framed as "people-dependent." The 2026 layer ties this to AI/ERP transformation: adoption capability as the thing that determines whether tech investment pays off.

**Verbatim narrative quotes:**
- *"Organizational change can only happen when individuals change."*
- *"Organizational changes often fail because employees don't understand the importance of getting on board the change or how to successfully make the change... And leaders are often not equipped to engage individuals effectively during the change and to manage any potential resistance."* (ADKAR page)
- *"changes such as technology deployments or new processes often fail because leaders and teams put too much focus on the technical aspects of the change. For successful change, organizations must also focus on the people side—and how to ensure that each individual embraces and adopts the change."* (Overview)
- *"The success of any organizational change depends on the success of change management in encouraging individuals to embrace, adopt and utilize a required change."* (Overview)
- *"43% of AI initiatives falter because workforce adoption and capabilities are lagging behind technology."* (Homepage)
- *"ERP success depends on more than system readiness—it depends on people readiness."* (Homepage)

- *"Prosci is a transformation partner for global enterprises"*
- *"Make your next transformation a success"*

- Microsoft testimonial: *"Change management creates a competitive advantage for our customers, and it achieves business outcomes and ROI at a greater rate than we would have seen otherwise... We call Prosci the global leader in the professional discipline of change management."*

**ADKAR page:**

## 5. Who They Talk To (Buyer)
The copy addresses a **layered enterprise audience**, not a single persona:
- **Change practitioners / change managers** — the certified operators ("Prosci Certified Change Practitioner," "change leaders," "change management teams"). This is the historic core buyer.
- **Executives / sponsors / leaders** — "we align leaders, prepare managers" — increasingly the primary enterprise buyer in the 2026 transformation framing (ERP, AI). Testimonials are from Directors and Sr. Managers of "Adoption & Change Management" at Microsoft, Avnet, Thermo Fisher.
- **Managers and employees** appear as the *subjects* to be guided, not the buyers.

Net: buyer = enterprise transformation sponsors + change management function leaders; HR is not the headlined audience.

## 6. Dominant Recurring Words / Phrases
"people side of change" · "adoption" / "adoption and usage" · "individual change" · "embrace, adopt and utilize/use" · "transformation" · "the global leader in change management" · "structured, adaptable, repeatable" · "barrier point" / "resistance" · "readiness" (people readiness / organizational readiness) · "outcomes" / "results" · "confidence" · "AI" and "ERP."
